sources.entry: gocron - Task scheduler that allows users to specify recurring jobs via a simple YAML configuration file. MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: GoCron is a self-hosted task scheduler that defines recurring shell-command jobs in a YAML file and manages runs, logs, and history through a web UI backed by SQLite.
summary.what_it_does: GoCron reads jobs from a YAML config file, each with a name, optional cron expression, commands, timeout, retries, and per-job environment variables, and runs them on schedule. Jobs inherit defaults such as cron, timeout, retries, env vars, and pre/post commands from a job_defaults block. A web UI lists jobs, triggers manual runs, streams logs over Server-Sent Events, and provides a terminal gated by an allow-list. Run history and logs are stored in SQLite, with optional automatic pruning after N days. The config file is watched and most changes apply without a restart. Optional features include HTTP healthcheck callbacks at job start, end, and failure, OIDC single sign-on, per-IP rate limiting, CORS settings, and installing tools such as restic or rclone at startup on Debian.
use_cases: schedule nightly backups with restic or rclone
run cron-style shell commands from a web UI
replace crontab with a YAML-defined scheduler
get alerted when scheduled jobs fail or do not run
trigger ad-hoc job runs and read their logs
protect a scheduler web UI with OIDC login
how_to_run: Or with Docker Compose: image ghcr.io/flohoss/gocron:latest, port 8156:8156, volume ./config/:/app/config/
Edit ./config/config.yaml to add jobs; changes are picked up automatically
Tagged GitHub releases include Linux binaries; run ./gocron_<version>_linux_<arch> --version to check the version
NixOS: services.gocron.enable = true, with settings in the nixpkgs module
notable: Single-flight scheduling: overlapping scheduled runs are skipped rather than queued
Config hot reload: most YAML changes apply without restart, with a single reload log line
Healthcheck HTTP callbacks at start, end, and failure, designed for Gatus heartbeat monitoring
Optional OIDC login using PKCE with DB-backed sessions; tested against Pocket-ID
Debian-only software installer for backup tools such as restic, borgbackup, rclone, and kopia
caveats: Software auto-install works only on Debian; it is skipped on other systems
Commands run as root by default in the published image, so least-privilege users must be configured for sensitive jobs
Without auth.oidc.enabled, the UI and API are open to anyone who can reach the port
Missed schedules are not caught up after the container is down; no @reboot support
Some settings (server address/port, rate limit, trusted proxies, database location, software) need a restart
